question: Does the worm's between-gene lead of the domain rule over nearest TSS survive EXCLUDING the elements that fall in outrons or in trans-splicing-affected 5' regions by the WormBase WS298 map -- the confound stage 1 registered as a caveat for this very stratum and never tested?
why_this_lane_exists: lane-flysource measured in Drosophila that the domain rule's lead over nearest TSS appears only where a host gene can be named and is absent between genes (+0.03 [-0.50, +0.60] on 789 elements, docs/SIMPLER-GENOMES.md section 11). The worm is NOT qualified by that: its between-gene stratum held at +3.73 [+2.79, +4.74] over 2,335 elements. But stage 1 registered a caveat for that very stratum -- trans-splicing and outrons -- and never tested it. This lane tests it.

candidates_considered.defines: operon|operon and dicistronic_mRNA|operon: operon spans with member WBGene ids (deprecated_operon is not used); SL1_acceptor_site and SL2_acceptor_site: measured trans-splice acceptor positions; TSS_region: WormBase's clustered transcription start site regions from the four published C. elegans TSS data sets (TSS_Chen, TSS_Kruesi, TSS_Saito, TSS_Gu in the WS298 TSS wiggle archive; WS298's release letter names WBPaper00042246, WBPaper00042529 and WBPaper00042354). Assembly WBcel235 (ce11), the same build as the Ensembl gene models stage 1 read; nothing is lifted over.
candidates_considered.assembly: WBcel235 (ce11); WormBase has used this build since WS235
candidates_considered.how: streamed from the EBI mirror and filtered in one pass to six feature classes; the 742 MB release file is not kept, the 8.0 MB extract is
candidates_considered.why_chosen: it is the only candidate that carries ALL THREE pieces the caveat needs -- WormBase's clustered TSS regions (which are the published Chen, Kruesi, Saito and Gu TSS data sets, Saito being the outron paper), the measured SL1 and SL2 trans-splice acceptor sites, and the operon annotation with member genes -- on the same assembly as the gene models stage 1 read, so nothing is lifted over
candidates_considered.licence: WormBase data are distributed for free reuse; the release, URL and WormBase's own published md5 are recorded instead of asserting a licence identifier this lane did not read, because wormbase.org/about/policies answered an unauthenticated fetch with HTTP 403 (Cloudflare)

candidates_considered.map: Saito et al. 2013 Genome Res 23:1348, supplementary TSS/outron tables
candidates_considered.why_not: WormBase's TSS_region features already carry this data set -- the WS298 TSS wiggle archive's members are TSS_Chen, TSS_Kruesi, TSS_Saito and TSS_Gu, and the release letter names WBPaper00042246, WBPaper00042529 and WBPaper00042354 -- on WBcel235, whereas the paper's own tables are on the build of 2013 and would need a liftover this lane could not verify

candidates_considered.map: Kruesi et al. 2013 eLife (GRO-cap TSSs); Chen et al. 2013 Genome Res; Gu et al.
candidates_considered.why_not: same reason: carried by WormBase's TSS_region features on WBcel235

the whole-file source|type census from the same pass

coordinates.note: both GFF3s are 1-based closed; the element midpoint is (start + end) // 2, and Table S2 does not state its base, so a midpoint moves by at most 1 bp either way

exclusions: elements with a host gene (domain_case == 'host'): the host stratum is not this lane's population
elements of any class other than putative_enhancer
elements whose tissue call is not exactly one of the five tissues
deprecated_operon features (111 of them), which WormBase no longer asserts
MtDNA, which carries no protein-coding gene in the models stage 1 read
the source table's own element-to-gene columns, which answer the question being asked
result_manifest.partitions: n/a: an inventory has no evaluation partition

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 7fb9087

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
